To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a unique solution to money-in-the-Utility-function models exists under measurability conditions, (2) the solution satisfies a stochastic Euler equation, and (3) the regularity conditions are economically innocuous.

(i) the necessary and sufficient condition for a unique solution to exist in money-in-the- utility- function models with uncertain asset returns is that the state variables be measurable with respect to a filtration that includes the information set at the time the utility function is evaluated; (ii) the existence of stochastic Euler equations is a consequence of the existence and uniqueness of the solution; and (iii) the regularity conditions required for these results to hold are economically innocuous.
